refuge

REF-yooj — starts like 'referee'; think 'refugee': a refuge is where you flee to be safe. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Refuge is a place or source of protection from danger or trouble.

The hikers took refuge in a cave when the storm rolled in.

Example

Hail suddenly pounds the mountain trail. A family spots an old ranger station, hurries inside, and bolts the door. In their refuge they wait out the storm safe and dry while ice hammers the roof.

The station shelters them from the storm's real danger. Unlike a 'hideout,' which conceals you from being found, a refuge protects you from harm.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shelter: A shelter is direct physical protection from weather or danger — a roof and walls between you and the storm. Refuge is wider: any place or source of protection, from a cave to a friend's kitchen. Every shelter can serve as a refuge, but a refuge need not be a building at all.

sanctuary: A sanctuary is a place set apart to stay safe permanently — originally a holy building where harm was not allowed to enter. A refuge is wherever you happen to find protection when danger arrives: any cellar or doorway can become one. Sanctuary is designated ahead of time; refuge is found in the moment.

haven: A haven is a place of safety and calm — the word looks forward to the comfort waiting once you arrive. Refuge looks back at the danger being escaped: you take refuge from a storm or a war. A haven promises rest; a refuge promises protection.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

exposure: the state of being unprotected

peril: serious danger

Where it sits · how strongly it guards against danger

retreat → refuge → fortress

retreat vs. refuge: A retreat is weaker than a refuge — it's a quiet place to withdraw for calm, not necessarily protection from real danger.

fortress vs. refuge: A fortress is stronger than a refuge: a refuge shelters you from danger, but a fortress is heavily defended against direct attack.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-: back, away (Latin)

root — fuge: to flee (Latin)

Put it together: Latin re- (back, away) plus fugere (to flee) gives 'a place you flee back to.' A refuge is where you run when fleeing away from danger.

Use the root in a new word: fugitive: The old poster in the sheriff's office still showed the fugitive's faded face.

Root Check

Word Choice

Refuge usually appears in the phrases 'take refuge' or 'seek refuge,' and can also name protected places like a wildlife refuge.
